ChangeJson.description: A single worktree/index change in JSON output.

old_path.description: Previous path for renames and copies (`null` when not applicable).

CommitJson.description: Shared commit object in JSON output (`log`, `show`, `revs`, `shortlog`, …).

change_id.description: Stable change id (reverse-hex; stored header or derived from commit id).

change_id_stored.description: `true` when `change_id` came from a `change-id` commit header.

message.description: Full message body with trailing whitespace trimmed.

refs.description: Ref decorations (branches, tags, `HEAD`, …) for this commit.

relative_date.description: Relative author date (e.g. `3 days ago`), when `now` is supplied.

CommitRefJson.description: Ref decoration attached to a commit in JSON output.

DivergenceChangeJson.description: One commit of a divergence: what each side did to it.

change.description: Its change id, or `patch:<patch id>` for a commit without one.

them.description: What they did to it, in the same words.

you.description: What you did to it: `unchanged`, `moved`, `reworded`, `amended`, `dropped`, `squashed`, `split`, `new`, `split_piece` or `absent`.

DivergenceJson.description: How another member's head diverged from yours ([`grit_lib::divergence`]).

also.description: Other scenarios that also apply, most pressing first.

base.description: The last head you both had, when known.

changes.description: The commits either side changed or added, oldest first.

conflicts.description: Paths where the two heads' changes conflict.

needs_decision.description: Whether someone has to decide what to do. When `false`, the heads can be put together without losing anything.

options.description: The ways out, the recommended one first.

scenario.description: The scenario's stable code, such as `amended_both_conflicting`.

GitButlerWorkspaceJson.description: A GitButler workspace in `grit status --json`: GitButler's merge of the applied branches.

commit.description: The workspace commit at the tip of `gitbutler/workspace` (full oid).

heads.description: The heads merged into the workspace, in its parent order.

HeadRelation.description: How another member's head compares with your branch here.

oneOf.description: It has commits yours doesn't, and yours is in its history: `grit sync` fast-forwards to it.
Yours has commits it doesn't, and it is in yours.
Each has commits the other lacks.
You have no branch here, or its commits aren't fetched.

InterruptedRewriteJson.description: Recovery of an interrupted rebase or history edit, in `--json` output.

oneOf.description: Refs had already moved: the checkout was completed and the rewrite stands.
The rewrite was undone: refs, index and files are back to their earlier state.
Another process holds `index.lock`; recovery runs on a later command.

alternatives.description: Mutually exclusive options (for example cancel the merge).

next_steps.description: Suggested follow-up commands, in order. A `git …` command appears only for an operation `git` started that grit cannot resume (for example `git rebase --continue`).

Person.description: A parsed identity line (`Name <email> <epoch> <tz>`) for stable `--json` output.

date.description: Author or committer timestamp in RFC 3339.

ResolveOptionJson.description: One way out of a divergence.

loses.description: What it leaves out (kept in the share's log), or `null` when it keeps every change: such an option is safe to choose without asking.

SharedHead.description: Another member's head of a shared branch.

divergence.description: For a head that diverged from yours: what happened, and whether someone has to decide what to do.

relation.description: How it compares with your branch here.

StatusSharedJson.description: A shared branch's other heads in `grit status`.

heads.description: Each other member's head, compared with this branch.

remote.description: The remote they were fetched from.

ahead.description: Commits on this branch not on the upstream, or `null` when counts were skipped.

behind.description: Commits on the upstream not on this branch, or `null` when counts were skipped.

SubmoduleChangeJson.description: Submodule detail on a gitlink change in status/diff JSON output.

WorkspaceHeadJson.description: One head merged into a GitButler workspace.

ahead.description: Commits on this head not on `target`, or `null` when counts were skipped or there is no target.

branches.description: Local branches that point at it, sorted; empty when none does.

ahead.description: Number of commits ahead of `target` (full count), or `null` when counts were skipped.

behind.description: Number of commits on `target` not in the current branch (full count), or `null` when skipped.

branch.description: Current branch (short name), or `null` when detached / invalid. While a rebase is in progress, the branch being rebased (`null` when the rebase started detached).

commits.description: Newest ahead-of-target commits (newest first), up to the status shortlog limit.

embedded_repositories.description: Untracked nested repositories that would be recorded as gitlinks if staged.

gitbutler_workspace.description: The GitButler workspace `HEAD` is on, when it is on one. `head` is then the workspace commit, and `commits` and `ahead` leave it out.

head.description: HEAD commit (full oid), or `null` on an unborn / invalid HEAD.

in_progress.description: In-progress operations (e.g. `merge`, `rebase`), when any apply. Deprecated: prefer `operation`.

interrupted_rewrite.description: What status did about a rebase or history edit that was killed after moving refs, when one was pending.

merging.description: True when a merge is in progress (`MERGE_HEAD` exists). Deprecated: prefer `operation`.

operation.description: Primary paused operation and suggested next commands.

shared.description: When the branch is shared (`grit share`): the other members' heads, as last fetched.

stash_count.description: Number of entries on the stash reflog.

target.description: Target branch name, or `null` when none applies / was found.

upstream.description: Upstream tracking comparison when it differs from `target`, or `null`.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings emitted while scanning the worktree (for example unreadable directories).
